correct_answer: The modification exceeded Hargrove's authority and the Teams thumbs-up from Patel does not constitute valid co-approval; the modification must be re-ratified by an officer with proper authority and a retroactive credit memo must be filed
rationale: The DOA Matrix v3.2 (effective 03/2025) is the operative version at the time of the modification (06/2025). Under this version, covenant waivers on classified assets (Risk Rating 6+) have a $2.0M cap and require Credit Risk Officer co-approval. The Meridian modification at $4.1M exceeds the $2.0M cap regardless of co-approval. Furthermore, the compliance review comment in ServiceNow explicitly states that a Teams thumbs-up does not meet documentation standards per Policy 12.1(b) — but also notes that a retroactive memo from Patel could cure the deficiency. The modification itself isn't void (Answer A is wrong — banks don't unwind modifications due to internal authority gaps; they remediate documentation), but it does need proper ratification. Answer A incorrectly applies the old DOA Matrix v2.8, which was superseded 3 months before the modification. Answer C incorrectly treats an informal emoji as meeting the formal co-approval documentation requirement. Answer A overstates the consequence — internal delegation breaches require remediation, not unwinding of customer-facing agreements.
